agreed_facts: For the three months ended May 31, 2026, total revenue increased 60% year over year to $8.222 million, EBITDA increased 29% to $4.685 million, net income increased 31% to $2.948 million, and diluted EPS increased to $0.12 from $0.09.
Water and wastewater revenue increased 119% year over year to $4.659 million, while water deliveries increased to 631 acre-feet from 76 acre-feet.
Lot sales revenue increased 19% year over year to $3.006 million from $2.526 million.
The company sold 66 water taps versus 40 and 48 wastewater taps versus 40 in the prior-year quarter.

Management expects Phase 2D to be substantially complete by the end of fiscal 2026, approximately 159 Phase 2E lots in fiscal 2027, and approximately $14.8 million of milestone and finished-lot payments over the next 12 months.
Management expects oil-and-gas water demand to continue through the remainder of 2026, and most of 23 contracted rental units are expected to come online during calendar 2026.
The current information does not establish whether the reported water volume or forward payment outlook is contracted, repeatable, or fully realized.

open_disagreements.topic: Durability of water and wastewater growth
open_disagreements.bull: The 119% revenue increase, large increase in water deliveries, and management's outlook for continued oil-and-gas demand indicate a durable and important growth engine.
open_disagreements.bear: The growth is unusually volume-sensitive because deliveries rose from 76 to 631 acre-feet; if deliveries normalize or oil-and-gas demand fades, the segment could weaken materially.
open_disagreements.what_would_resolve: PCYO's next Form 10-Q or Form 10-K, including segment revenue and delivery-volume tables, customer or end-market concentration disclosures, and any disclosed backlog, purchase commitments, or contracted acre-feet; corroborating oil-and-gas demand data from Colorado's Colorado Oil and Gas Conservation Commission production and permit datasets would also test the demand outlook.

open_disagreements.topic: Whether the $14.8 million of expected payments represents reliable near-term monetization
open_disagreements.bull: The stated milestone and finished-lot payment outlook provides visible revenue and cash-flow support over the next 12 months.
open_disagreements.bear: The amount is forward-looking and depends on construction, contractual milestones, closing timing, and builder execution, so it is not yet equivalent to realized revenue.
open_disagreements.what_would_resolve: The next PCYO Form 10-Q and subsequent Form 10-K, together with the Sky Ranch development agreement or a filed material-contract exhibit, showing payment schedules, remaining conditions, recognized revenue, receivables, deposits, and actual cash collections against the $14.8 million outlook.

open_disagreements.topic: Builder absorption and the pace of Phase 2E lot monetization
open_disagreements.bull: Phase 2D completion and the planned 159 Phase 2E lots create visible execution catalysts, with pacing to absorption presented as disciplined delivery rather than a fundamental problem.
open_disagreements.bear: The explicit decision to pace Phase 2E lots to builder absorption indicates demand may constrain future deliveries and could limit the timing of lot revenue.
open_disagreements.what_would_resolve: The next quarterly filing and the company's next earnings-call transcript or investor presentation, specifically disclosing Phase 2D and 2E lot deliveries, contracted or sold lots, builder inventory, cancellations, backlog, and absorption rates; Arapahoe County's publicly posted single-family permit dataset would independently test local housing demand.

open_disagreements.topic: Interpretation of the unchanged earnings model
open_disagreements.bull: The unchanged model is consistent with a solid reported quarter and does not itself signal deteriorating fundamentals.
open_disagreements.bear: Leaving net income, EBITDA, and EPS unchanged may indicate the model does not incorporate downside from lower water volumes or execution risk, limiting the significance of the headline beat.
open_disagreements.what_would_resolve: The analyst's published post-earnings model update or valuation note, if public, showing revised revenue, volume, margin, and EPS assumptions; absent that, PCYO's next filing and management's disclosed sensitivity or segment-margin data would show whether actual results are converting into durable forecast changes.

data.summary: Both sides agree that PCYO reported broad-based year-over-year growth, led by water and wastewater, alongside higher lot sales, tap volumes, and stated Phase 2D, Phase 2E, rental, and payment milestones. The unresolved issues are whether the water surge and oil-and-gas demand are repeatable, whether the $14.8 million outlook will be realized on schedule, and whether builder absorption or model assumptions constrain future results.
